extracted.intended_audience: patent attorneys, applicants, Patent Office officials, and litigators dealing with UK patent law (practitioners applying the statutes)
extracted.subtask_description: Interpretation and operational rules from the UK patent statutes covering prosecution, office procedure, remedies, secrecy, international priority, offences, and transitional provisions. Useful for practitioners ensuring compliance with statutory requirements and court practice under the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delivery of particulars when disputing validity
rubrics_metrics.description: If the defendant disputes the validity of the patent, the ... by him must state on what grounds he disputes, and, if one of those grounds is want of novelty, must state the time and place of the previous publication or user alleged by him.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Particulars of objections/defences must be delivered in the prescribed manner. At the hearing, evidence in proof of any alleged infringement or objection of which particulars were not delivered shall not be admitted except by leave of the Court or a judge. Particulars may be amended from time to time by leave of the Court or a judge. On taxation of costs regard shall be had to the particulars delivered by both parties; no costs shall be allowed in respect of any particular unless certified by the Court or a judge to have been proven or to have been reasonable and proper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissibility of evidence tied to particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: At the hearing no evidence shall, except by leave of the Court or a judge, be admitted in proof of any alleged infringement or objection of which particulars are not so delivered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This links pleading/delivery requirements to evidence: failure to provide particulars generally bars admission of evidence on that point unless the Court allows it. Parties should ensure timely, detailed particulars to preserve evidence and costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment of particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: Particulars delivered may be from time to time amended by leave of the Court or a judge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts have discretion to permit amendments; practitioners should apply promptly to amend when new facts arise and be prepared to justify amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Taxation of costs regards particulars
rubrics_metrics.description: On taxation of costs regard shall be had to the particulars delivered by the plaintiff and by the defendant; and they, respectively, shall not be allowed any costs in respect of any particular delivered by them unless the same is certified by the Court or a judge to have been proven or to have been reasonable and proper.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Delivery of unfounded particulars may lead to refusal of costs. Seek certification from the Court that particulars were proven or reasonable to secure costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court's powers to order injunction, inspection, or account
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement of a patent, the Court or a judge may, on the application of either party, make such order for an injunction, inspection, or account, and impose such terms, and give such directions respecting the same and the proceedings thereon as the Court or a judge may see fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedies are discretionary and may include ancillary directions/terms. Parties should specify the relief sought and proposed terms in applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification that validity came in question and cost consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: In an action for infringement of a patent, the Court or a judge may certify that the validity of the patent came in question; and if so certified then, in any subsequent action for infringement, the plaintiff on obtaining a final order or judgment in his favour shall have his full costs, charges, and expenses as between solicitor and client, unless the Court or judge trying the action certifies that he ought not to have the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'validity came in question' certificate in one action can affect costs in later proceedings; it incentivises raising bona fide validity issues and gives winners potential enhanced costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Action for groundless threats (misuse of threat of proceedings)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any person claiming to be the patentee threatens any other person with legal proceedings or liability in respect of alleged manufacture, use, sale, or purchase, any person aggrieved may bring an action and may obtain an injunction against continuance of such threats, and may recover damages, if the alleged activity was not in fact an infringement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The section does not apply if the person making the threats with due diligence commences and prosecutes an action for infringement. This creates a remedy against unjustified threats but protects bona fide enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent form and single-invention rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Every patent may be in the form in the First Schedule to this Act, and shall be granted for one invention only, but may contain more than one claim; but it shall not be competent for any person in an action or other proceeding to take any objection to a patent on the ground that it comprises more than one invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although patents are to be granted for one invention, multiple claims are permitted and the presence of multiple claims is not a ground for objection in proceedings. Draft claims accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application by legal representative after inventor's death
rubrics_metrics.description: If a person possessed of an invention dies without making application for a patent, application may be made by his legal representative; every such application must be made within six months of the decease and must contain a declaration by the legal representative that he believes such person to be the true and first inventor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timeliness (six months) and the required declaration are mandatory. Executors/administrators should act promptly after inventor's death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent not invalidated by an application in fraud or provisional protection
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent granted to the true and first inventor shall not be invalidated by an application in fraud of him, or by provisional protection obtained thereon, or by any use or publication of the invention subsequent to that fraudulent application during the period of provisional protection.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This protects the rights of true inventors from being defeated by prior fraudulent filings by others; relevant when assessing validity challenges alleging intervening acts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment to extend territorial effect
rubrics_metrics.description: A patentee may assign his patent for any place in or part of the United Kingdom, or Isle of Man, as effectually as if the patent were originally granted to extend to that place or part only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assignments may be limited territorially; ensure assignments specify territorial extent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate patent when lost or destroyed
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent is lost or destroyed, or its non-production accounted for to the satisfaction of the Comptroller, the Comptroller may at any time cause a duplicate thereof to be sealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedure exists for replacement of lost/destroyed patent documents on proof to Comptroller's satisfaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Law officers' powers re witnesses, rules, and costs orders
rubrics_metrics.description: The law officers may examine witnesses on oath and administer oaths under this part of this Act, may make, alter, and rescind rules regulating references and appeals to the law officers and practice before them; in any proceeding before either, the law officer may order costs to be paid by either party and any such order may be made a rule of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Law officers have investigatory and rule-making powers and may determine costs in proceedings before them; practitioners should be prepared for references and possible costs orders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibition disclosure does not prejudice patent rights (conditions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The exhibition of an invention at an industrial or international exhibition certified by the Board of Trade, or the publication/use of any description of the invention during the period of the holding of the exhibition, shall not prejudice the right to apply for provisional protection and a patent, provided: (a) the exhibitor gives the Comptroller the prescribed notice of his intention before exhibiting; and (b) the application for a patent is made before or within six months from the date of the opening of the exhibition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To rely on the exhibition exception, give the prescribed notice to the Comptroller before exhibition and apply within six months. Otherwise public exhibition may be novelty-destroying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's publication and indexing duties
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller shall cause to be issued periodically an illustrated journal of patented inventions, reports of patent cases decided by courts, and any other information deemed generally useful; shall keep copies of the journal and all complete specifications for sale; shall continue indexes and abridgments and prepare other indexes, abridgments, catalogues, and works relating to inventions as he sees fit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patent Office publications and indexes are official sources; practitioners can rely on certified copies and official indexes for evidence and searching.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Museum control and model requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The control and management of the existing Patent Museum shall be transferred to the Department of Science and Art. The Department may require a patentee to furnish a model of his invention on payment of the cost of manufacture of the model; the amount to be settled, in case of dispute, by the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Patentees may be required to provide models for museum purposes with the Patent Office (Dept of Science & Art) reimbursing manufacture costs; disputes resolved by Board of Trade.

rubrics_metrics.name: Navigation exception for foreign vessels
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent shall not prevent the use of an invention for the purposes of the navigation of a foreign vessel within the jurisdiction of any of Her Majesty's Courts in the United Kingdom or Isle of Man, or the use of an invention in a foreign vessel within that jurisdiction, provided it is not used therein for or in connection with the manufacture or preparation of anything intended to be sold in or exported from the United Kingdom or Isle of Man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Limited exception allowing use on foreign vessels in domestic jurisdiction for navigation purposes only; does not extend to vessels of foreign states whose laws permit subjects to prevent such use of inventions in British vessels in their ports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignment of munitions/war inventions to Secretary of State
rubrics_metrics.description: The inventor of any improvement in instruments or munitions of war may assign to Her Majesty's Principal Secretary of State for the War Department all the benefit of the invention and of any patent obtained or to be obtained; the assignment shall vest the benefit in the Secretary of State and covenants for secrecy/enforcement shall be valid and effectual notwithstanding any want of valuable consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special assignment regime for war-related inventions permits assignment to the Crown and enforces secrecy covenants even without consideration; assignments can be enforced by Secretary of State.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secrecy certification and sealed-packet procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Secretary of State certifies that, in the interest of the public service, particulars of the invention and of the manner in which it is to be performed should be kept secret, the application and specifications, drawings, and any amendments shall be delivered to the Comptroller in a packet sealed by authority of the Secretary; such packet shall be kept sealed until expiration of the term or extended term and shall not be opened save under authority of the Secretary of State or the law officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed-packet handling replaces ordinary Patent Office deposit and publication for national-security matters. Such sealed material is not open to public inspection; provisions govern delivery to authorised persons and eventual release after patent term expiry or by written authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of secrecy certification (no revocation, non-publication)
rubrics_metrics.description: No proceeding by petition or otherwise shall lie for revocation of a patent granted for an invention in relation to which the Secretary of State has certified as aforesaid. No copy of any specification or other document required to be placed in a sealed packet shall be published or open to the inspection of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Secrecy certification removes normal revocation route and prevents publication of specifications; the Secretary may waive the benefit of secrecy for particular inventions by writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Communications to Secretary re munitions not treated as publication/use
rubrics_metrics.description: The communication of any invention for improvement in instruments or munitions of war to the Secretary of State, or to any person authorised to investigate the same, shall not, nor shall anything be done for the purposes of the investigation, be deemed use or publication of such invention so as to prejudice the grant or validity of any patent for the same.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosures to government for investigation purposes are protected from destroying novelty/validity — relevant for inventors submitting to defense authorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of the Act to existing patents (transitional provisions)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this Act relating to applications for patents and proceedings thereon shall have effect in respect only of applications made after the commencement of this Act. Every patent granted before the commencement of this Act, or on an application then pending, shall remain unaffected by provisions relating to patents binding the Crown and to compulsory licences. In all other respects (including the amount and time of payment of fees) this Act shall extend to all patents granted before the commencement or on application then pending, in substitution for such enactments as would have applied thereto.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transitional rules determine which parts of the new Act apply to pre-existing patents/applications. Check which provisions are expressly preserved or substituted when advising holders of older patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (patent, patentee, invention)
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of this Act— 'Patent' means letters patent for an invention; 'Patentee' means the person for the time being entitled to the benefit of a patent; 'Invention' means any manner of new manufacture the subject of letters patent and grant of privilege within section six of the Statute of Monopolies and includes an alleged invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory definitions guide interpretation throughout the Act; 'invention' defined by reference to 'new manufacture' and historical statute — implications for novelty/non-technical inventions should be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment and control of the Patent Office and Comptroller-General
rubrics_metrics.description: The Treasury may provide an office called the Patent Office. The Patent Office shall be under the immediate control of an officer called the Comptroller-General of Patents, Designs, and Trade Marks, who shall act under the superintendence and direction of the Board of Trade. Any act or thing directed to be done by or to the Comptroller may, in his absence, be done by or to any officer authorised by the Board of Trade.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organisational structure and delegation: Board of Trade/Treasury powers, and delegation within the Office, are set by statute — practitioners must address filings and communications to the proper officer or authorised delegate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointments, salaries, and funding for Patent Office staff
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Trade may appoint the Comptroller-General, examiners, and other officers and clerks, and may remove them; their salaries shall be appointed by the Board with concurrence of the Treasury, and the expense of executing the Act shall be paid out of money provided by Parliament.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative staffing and remuneration are statutory; impacts on fee-setting and governance; not typically a direct litigation matter but relevant to office functioning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Seal of the Patent Office judicially noticed
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be a seal for the Patent Office, and impressions thereof shall be judicially noticed and admitted in evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Sealed Patent Office copies are official evidence in court; use certified sealed copies when possible to avoid need for originals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller may refuse patents contrary to law or morality
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller may refuse to grant a patent for an invention, or to register a design or trade mark, of which the use would, in his opinion, be contrary to law or morality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative refusals can be grounded in public policy/morality considerations; applicants should be prepared to address grounds and seek review where appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry of proprietor on proof of title and proprietor's powers
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a person becomes entitled by assignment, transmission, or other operation of law to a patent, the Comptroller shall, on request and on proof of title to his satisfaction, enter the name of such person as proprietor of the patent in the Register of Patents. The person so entered shall have power to assign, grant licences as to, or otherwise deal with the same, and to give effectual receipts for any consideration; equities may be enforced as in respect of other personal property.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registration of proprietor is evidential and confers ability to deal with patent; ensure proof of title meets Comptroller's standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Registers open to public subject to regulations; certified copies for fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Every register kept under this Act shall at all convenient times be open to inspection of the public, subject to the provisions of this Act and regulations; certified copies sealed with the Patent Office seal of any entry shall be given to any person requiring the same on payment of the prescribed fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public inspection and certified copies are available but subject to rules — secrecy/sealed-packet exceptions apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sealed certified copies admissible in evidence without further proof
rubrics_metrics.description: Printed or written copies or extracts purporting to be certified by the Comptroller and sealed with the Patent Office seal of or from patents, specifications, disclaimers, and other documents shall be admitted in evidence in all courts without further proof or production of the originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use certified sealed copies to streamline proof in litigation; they are prima facie evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court power to rectify registers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court may, on application of any person aggrieved by omission without sufficient cause or by any entry made without sufficient cause, make such order for making, expunging, or varying the entry as the Court thinks fit, may decide necessary questions, may direct an issue to be tried for decision of questions of fact, and may award damages to the party aggrieved. Any order rectifying a register shall direct that due notice of the rectification be given to the Comptroller.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Court-ordered rectifications provide a remedy for incorrect register entries; parties should seek rectification orders with supporting evidence and be aware of costs/discretionary relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's power to correct clerical errors
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller may, on request in writing accompanied by the prescribed fee, correct any clerical error in or in connection with an application for a patent; or correct any clerical error in the name, style, or address of the registered proprietor of a patent; and correct entry of a trade mark on the register on request by statutory declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is an administrative route to correct clerical mistakes without court proceedings; follow prescribed forms/fees and provide statutory declarations where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: False entries or forged copies punishable as misdemeanor
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person makes or causes to be made a false entry in any register kept under this Act, or a writing falsely purporting to be a copy of an entry, or produces or tenders a writing knowing it to be false, he shall be guilty of a misdemeanor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strict criminal sanction for false documents; ensure authenticity of filings and copies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to be heard before adverse exercise of Comptroller's power
rubrics_metrics.description: Where any power is by this Act given to the Comptroller, he shall not exercise that power adversely to the applicant for a patent, or for amendment of a specification, without, if so required within the time by the applicant, giving the applicant an opportunity of being heard personally or by his agent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedural fairness required before adverse administrative action; applicants must request opportunity to be heard within prescribed times.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Office entries/acts as prima facie evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: A certificate purporting to be under the hand of the Comptroller as to any matter he is authorised to make or do shall be prima-facie evidence of the entry having been made and of the contents thereof, and of the matter or thing having been done or left undone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comptroller's certificates carry evidential weight; rebuttable, but useful in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by post deemed service; proof by proper addressing and posting
rubrics_metrics.description: Any application, notice or other document required to be left, made, or given at the Patent Office or to the Comptroller may be sent by prepaid letter through the post; if so sent it shall be deemed to have been left, made or given at the time when the letter would be delivered in the ordinary course of post. In proving such service it suffices to prove the letter was properly addressed and put into the post.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Postal service rules govern deemed filing dates; ensure correct addressing and proof of posting to rely on deemed delivery.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excluded days extension for filing and fee payment
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever the last day fixed by this Act, or by any rule in force, for leaving any document or paying any fee at the Patent Office shall fall on Christmas day, Friday, Saturday, Sunday, Bank Holiday, or any day observed as public fast or thanksgiving (excluded days), it shall be lawful to leave such document or to pay such fee on the day next following such excluded day.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practical extension of deadlines where they fall on excluded days; use the next business day for filings/fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Substitutes for incapable persons may act
rubrics_metrics.description: If any person is, by reason of infancy, lunacy, or other inability, incapable of making any declaration or doing anything required or permitted by this Act, then the guardian or committee, or if none, any person appointed by a Court, may make such declaration or do such thing in the name and on behalf of such incapable person, and all acts done by such substitute shall be as effectual as if done by the person substituted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statutory provision for representation of legally incapable persons in patent matters; ensure appointment/order exists when acting on their behalf.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transmission of accepted/allowed specifications to other offices
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of all specifications, drawings, and amendments left at the Patent Office after commencement of this Act, printed and sealed with the Patent Office seal, shall be transmitted to the Edinburgh Museum of Science and Art, the Enrolments Office of the Chancery Division in Ireland, and to the Rolls Office in the Isle of Man, within twenty-one days after the same have been accepted or allowed at the Patent Office; certified copies or extracts shall be given to any person requiring the same on payment of the prescribed fee and shall be admitted in evidence in all Courts in Scotland and Ireland and in the Isle of Man without further proof or production of the originals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regional transmission and admissibility rules ensure access and evidential effect across jurisdictions; certified copies available on payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade rule-making powers and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board of Trade may from time to time make general rules for regulating the practice of registration, for classifying goods for designs and trade marks, for making or requiring duplicates of specifications, drawings and other documents, for securing and regulating publishing and selling of copies and indexes, for presentation of copies of Patent Office publications to patentees and public authorities, and generally for regulating the business of the Patent Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broad delegated rule-making power governs procedural detail; check current Board of Trade/Patent Office rules for practice directions and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure for making/amending rules and parliamentary oversight
rubrics_metrics.description: Any rules made under this section shall be laid before both Houses of Parliament and advertised; if either House resolves within forty days that such rules ought to be annulled they become of no effect, without prejudice to actions done in the meantime.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules are subject to parliamentary scrutiny and potential annulment—practitioners should track rules published in official Journal and be aware of possible changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comptroller's annual report
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comptroller shall, before the first day of June in every year, cause a report respecting the execution of this Act to be laid before both Houses of Parliament, and shall include all general rules made in that year and an account of all fees, salaries, allowances and other money received and paid under this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Annual reports publicise administrative practice, fee income, and rule changes — useful source for practitioners tracking procedural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Board of Trade and its officers may act in proceedings; their documents admissible
rubrics_metrics.description: All things required or authorised to be done by, to, or before the Board of Trade may be done by the President or a secretary or assistant-secretary; documents purporting to be orders made by the Board and sealed, or signed by authorised persons, shall be received in evidence and deemed such orders without further proof; a certificate signed by the President that any order made or act done is that of the Board shall be conclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative acts and certificates from Board of Trade carry conclusive evidential weight unless challenged; rely on these in dealings with the Patent Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: International priority from foreign application (arrangements)
rubrics_metrics.description: If Her Majesty makes arrangements with any foreign Government for mutual protection of inventions, any person who has applied for protection for an invention in such state shall be entitled to a patent under this Act in priority to other applicants and such patent shall have the same date as the date of the application in such foreign state, provided his application is made within seven months from his applying for protection in the foreign state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Priority based on corresponding foreign filing within seven months preserves novelty despite intervening publication/use in the UK during the priority period; application must be made in the same manner as ordinary applications and applies only to states declared by Order in Council.

rubrics_metrics.name: Colonial and Indian application of provisions by Order in Council
rubrics_metrics.description: If it appears the colonies and India have made satisfactory provision for protection of inventions, it shall be lawful for Her Majesty by Order in Council to apply the provisions of the Act (with variations/additions as fit) to such British Possessions; an Order shall take effect as if contained in the Act and may be revoked by Her Majesty in Council.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Extension to colonies is by Order in Council; check applicable Orders for colonial/Indian patent law variations and revocations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence — falsely representing an article as patented
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who represents that any article sold by him is a patented article, when no patent has been granted for the same, shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding five pounds. A person shall be deemed to represent an article is patented if he sells the article with the word 'patent', 'patented', or any words expressing or implying a patent, stamped on or otherwise applied to the article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criminal/sanctioned offence for false patent claims on goods; avoid labelling products as 'patented' unless a patent exists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Offence — unauthorised use of royal arms
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person who, without authority of Her Majesty or any Government Department, assumes or uses in connection with any trade, business, calling, or profession, the royal arms or arms so nearly resembling the same as to be calculated to deceive, shall be liable on summary conviction to a fine not exceeding twenty pounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of royal insignia in trade without authority is penalised; ensure proper permissions for such use.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scotland: infringement procedure and no-jury trial default
rubrics_metrics.description: In any action for infringement of a patent in Scotland the provisions with respect to calling in the aid of an assessor shall apply, and the action shall be tried without a jury unless the Court shall otherwise direct; otherwise nothing shall affect the jurisdiction and forms of process of the Courts in Scotland in such an action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scots procedure varies (no jury by default; assessors may be called). Practitioners should follow Scottish procedural forms and consult Lord Advocate concurrence requirements for revocation actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scotland: prosecution of summary offences and revocation proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Any offence under this Act declared to be summary punishable may be prosecuted in the Sheriff Court. Proceedings in Scotland for revocation of a patent shall be in the form of an action of reduction at the instance of the Lord Advocate, or at the instance of a party having interest with his concurrence which may be given on just cause shown only; service of writs and summonses shall be made according to forms and practice existing at commencement of this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special rules apply for revocation in Scotland including requirement of Lord Advocate involvement or his concurrence; service follows pre-existing Scottish forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ireland: remedies and reservation
rubrics_metrics.description: All parties shall, notwithstanding anything in this Act, have in Ireland their remedies under or in respect of a patent as if the same had been granted to extend to Ireland only.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Irish remedies retained as if patents extended to Ireland only; check local practice and any reservation clauses when advising in Ireland.

rubrics_metrics.name: General jurisdiction clause (Scotland/Ireland)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions conferring a special jurisdiction on the Court as defined by this Act shall not, except so far as the jurisdiction extends, affect the jurisdiction of any Court in Scotland or Ireland in any proceedings relating to patents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Jurisdictional boundaries preserved: UK-wide patent jurisdiction does not oust Scottish or Irish courts outside the statutory extent.
